entry.title: Network Menu Speed Test 1.0
entry.content:
Network Menu Speed Test

Windows 11's network menu ("Run internet speed test") opens

https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2324916

in the default browser, which redirects to a Bing search page.

This mod intercepts that URL in the shell processes and replaces it with a native flyout. The window, the gauge, the result cards and the speed measurement all live inside the mod: no external application or protocol handler is involved. The test talks to the public Cloudflare speed test endpoints (speed.cloudflare.com), the same stateless endpoints used by the website.

Screenshots

Light theme Dark theme
Desktop Acrylic Results card

Data usage

The test transfers real data with a per-direction budget of 512 MB. Lines at or below ~340 Mbps complete the full 12 s window per direction without reaching the budget; faster lines end the phase once the budget is spent (minimum 4 s window, and the result divides bytes by the time the transfer was actually moving data). Total usage stays under ~1 GB regardless of line speed, and the results card shows the bytes used ("Data used: 762 MB", also included in the clipboard text).

The Start the test automatically setting defaults to auto: the test starts when the flyout opens, except when Windows reports the connection as metered - then the flyout opens idle and waits for a click on Start.

Coexistence: the mod perform-speedtest-redirect intercepts the same URL launches. If both are enabled, whichever mod hooks the launch first wins - disable the other one to keep this mod's flyout.

The flyout opens above the taskbar, on the monitor under the mouse. It closes when you click outside, but never while a measurement is running.

It is keyboard accessible (Tab / Enter / Esc with a WinUI-style focus ring), exposed to screen readers through MSAA (WM_GETOBJECT), and honours the "Animation effects" system setting: with animations off every transition is instant. The error view shrinks the window to fit its content.

Settings

  • Extra URL patterns: additional substrings separated by |.
  • Fall back to the web page: if the flyout cannot start, run the original URL instead of doing nothing.
  • Also intercept browser process launches: catch the network menu launching the browser directly through CreateProcessW. The launch returns ERROR_CANCELLED because no browser process is created; turning it off makes the menu open the browser normally when the shell skips the shell-execute path.
  • Start the test automatically: auto starts the test when the flyout opens, but waits for a click when Windows reports the connection as metered; always starts unconditionally; never always waits for a click.
  • Language: auto (follows the Windows display language), it or en.

Diagnostics go to the Windhawk mod log: enable logging for this mod from its Details page in Windhawk when you need them.

Note: when the network menu launches the browser directly through CreateProcessW, the flyout is shown but process creation returns ERROR_CANCELLED: the hook never reports success without creating the requested browser process.

entry.title: Bluetooth No Sleep 1.0.0
entry.content:
Bluetooth No Sleep (Bluetooth Audio Keep-Alive)

A lightweight Windows background utility and Windhawk tool mod that prevents Bluetooth audio devices (headphones, wireless earbuds, soundbars, DACs, and speakers) from falling asleep, dropping initial playback, or disconnecting during silence.

Why this mod?

Modern Bluetooth audio peripherals employ aggressive power-saving timers:

  1. Initial Audio Truncation: When no audio plays for a few seconds, the device enters a low-power state and shuts off its internal DAC/amplifier. When audio resumes, waking up takes 1-2 seconds, dropping the beginning of system notifications, speech, or media playback.
  2. Pops and Static Bursts: Rapid DAC wakeups often create audible transients, clicks, or static bursts ("pink noise").
  3. Unsolicited Idle Disconnections: Many wireless devices shut down completely after 5 to 10 minutes of silence, forcing manual power cycling.

How it works

This mod uses Windows Audio Session API (WASAPI) Shared Mode to continuously stream an inaudible digital silence buffer (0x00 PCM or sub-audible dither) to the active audio endpoint:

  • Non-Intrusive Shared Mode: Runs alongside your normal applications without monopolizing or locking audio devices.
  • Event-Driven Endpoint Tracking: Uses IMMNotificationClient to monitor device transitions. When your default audio device switches or a Bluetooth headset reconnects, it rebinds automatically without crashes.
  • Near-Zero CPU Overhead: Uses buffer-synchronized wait events and sleep cycles to keep CPU usage below 0.1%.
  • Optional Inactivity Gate: Can automatically pause the keep-alive stream after prolonged user inactivity to allow intentional battery conservation and permit normal Windows system sleep (powercfg /requests).
  • Dedicated Tool Mod: Runs inside windhawk.exe as a dedicated background tool without injecting into or hooking any system processes.

entry.title: Explorer Core Context Menu Customizer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Core Context Menu Customizer

Windows does not provide any registry entries or built-in options to customize the icons or labels of core File Explorer context menu commands. This mod was created to fill that gap cleanly and safely.

Windows 11 Note: This mod customizes the classic File Explorer context menu (accessible via Show more options or Shift+F10, or when the classic context menu is enabled).

Screenshots:

Disabled (Default) Enabled (Customized)

Highlights:

  • Canonical Verb Matching: Identifies core shell commands via IContextMenu::GetCommandString (GCS_VERBW), working across every Windows display language without touching third-party shell extension items.
  • Zero Layout Distortion: Attaches icons cleanly during IContextMenu::QueryContextMenu so native row height, padding, and bold text remain completely untouched.
  • Clear-to-Reset Behavior: Clearing an icon path removes the icon for Open, Delete, Rename, or Properties, while Run as administrator reverts to the native Windows UAC shield.
  • Custom Icon Support: Easily add your own .ico files or use any built-in Windows icon with dll,index syntax.
  • Per-Monitor DPI & Leak-Free Caching: Caches 32-bpp ARGB bitmaps per monitor DPI in memory with zero GDI handle leaks.

Dynamic %file% Placeholder:

Include %file% (or %name%) in any custom label field to dynamically display the right-clicked file, folder, or shortcut target name. Names longer than 30 characters are automatically shortened to the first 30 characters followed by ...:

  • Rename: '%file%' -> Rename: 'Spotify.exe'
  • Open: %file% -> Open: New folder (2)
  • Delete %file% -> Delete Very_Long_File_Name_Over_Thirt...
  • %file% Properties -> report.pdf Properties

Supported Context Menu Items:

  1. Open (open) - Top bold default action (default icon: imageres.dll,-185)
  2. Run as administrator (runas) - UAC elevation action (keeps native UAC shield and default label unless customized)
  3. Delete (delete) - File and folder deletion action (default icon: Full Recycle Bin imageres.dll,-54)
  4. Rename (rename) - Inline rename action (default icon: Clipboard shell32.dll,-16763, default label: Rename: '%file%')
  5. Properties (properties) - Bottom item details action (default icon: imageres.dll,-114)

entry.title: Flip3DComp 2.0
entry.content:
Flip3DComp

Original version by: ALTaleX531

A DirectComposition reimplementation of the Flip3D Window switcher introduced on Windows Vista, for newer versions of Windows. Ported from my repository Flip3DComp

Demo

Live window previews follow the original Flip3D carousel layout and timing.

Requirements

  • Windows 10 versions 1703 and higher
  • Windhawk 1.7.3 or higher

⚠️ Notes

  • The optional Task View override currently uses the Windows 11 Task View activation path on AMD64. It is unavailable on x86, ARM64 & Windows 10.
  • Do not enable more than one Win+Tab replacement. Disable Any mods that override Win+Tab, or leave Win+Tab disabled in Alt+Tab Flip 3D, while using Flip3DComp.

Controls

  • Win+Tab: Open Flip3D
  • Ctrl + Win + Tab: Open Flip3D in Sticky Mode
  • Tab / Shift + Tab, arrow keys, mouse wheel: scroll the carousel
  • Enter or left click a card: activate the selected window
  • Home: return to the original front window
  • Esc: exit
  • F5: replay the enter animation

Mod disclosure

  • Unlike the existing Flip 3D mods in the Windhawk catalog, this mod is a reimplementation of the original Windows Vista Flip 3D, built on DirectComposition.

entry.title: Glass Widget Bar 0.3.0
entry.content:
Glass Widget Bar

A desktop widget bar that sits in a frosted-glass frame: the blurred wallpaper shows through a soft, dark-tinted rounded panel with thin light edges. The widgets have no glass of their own; they are drawn straight onto the frame and separated by thin dividers.

Widget What it does
Clock Analog clock with an orange second hand
Calendar Weekday, large day number, month grid; today is highlighted in red
Music The track that is playing right now (Spotify, browser, Media Player...), cover art, progress and ⏮ ⏯ ⏭ buttons

Languages

Labels, day names and month names follow your Windows display language automatically. You can also pick a language in the settings.

English, Türkçe, Deutsch, Français, Español, Italiano, Português (Brasil), Nederlands, Polski, Русский, Українська, Čeština, Svenska, Dansk, Norsk bokmål, Suomi, Ελληνικά, Magyar, Română, Български, Bahasa Indonesia, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, हिन्दी, 日本語, 한국어, 简体中文, 繁體中文.

Other display languages fall back to English. The first day of the week in the calendar follows your Windows regional format (or the chosen language). Right-to-left languages are not supported yet. The translations are machine-assisted, corrections are welcome.

Notes

  • The default layer is the desktop: windows cover the bar. Press the hotkey (default Ctrl+Alt+W) to bring it to the front (press again to send it back), or set "Always on top" in the settings.
  • The hotkey, its modifier keys and its key can be changed or turned off in the settings. Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so if your keyboard layout types characters with AltGr, pick a combination without Alt. If another app already owns the combination it cannot be registered; the Windhawk log then says so.
  • Works on the primary monitor only. A picture wallpaper is expected.
  • The defaults of the frame (opacity 15, blur 10) match the dock mod this frame comes from. If your wallpaper is very bright, raise the opacity.
  • The music widget reads the Windows media session, so every app that publishes one is shown.
  • Developed on Windows 11 (64-bit).

Credits and license

The frame (rounded "squircle" corners, edge glow and edge lines) is ported from MacOS Style Dock by Zach Vaughn (GPL-3.0). This mod is therefore released under GPL-3.0 as well.

entry.title: Color Picker / Eyedropper Tool 1.0.2
entry.content:
Color Picker / Eyedropper Tool for Windows 11

A lightweight, system-wide color picker overlay mod for Windhawk, inspired by Microsoft PowerToys Color Picker. Activated by the default keyboard shortcut Win + Alt + C, it allows you to select any pixel on your screen via a customizable global hotkey, view a magnified pixel grid loupe, and automatically obtain the color value in HEX, RGB, HSL, and CMYK formats with one-click clipboard copying.

Features

  • System-Wide Screen Freeze & Overlay: Freezes the screen upon activation to prevent accidental click-throughs onto underlying windows.
  • Magnified Loupe Cursor: Displays a magnified preview grid with a centered crosshair and a live color preview badge that follows your cursor.
  • Multi-Format Support: Automatically converts and displays captured colors in:
    • HEX (e.g., #FF5733 or ff5733)
    • RGB (e.g., rgb(255, 87, 51))
    • HSL (e.g., hsl(11, 100%, 60%))
    • CMYK (e.g., cmyk(0%, 66%, 80%, 0%))
  • Native Windows 11 Dark Mode Support: The result pop-up window automatically adapts to your system theme (Light or Dark mode).
  • Modern UI Styling: Clean, dialog-style UI using Segoe UI font, smooth rounded corners, drop-shadow effects, and single-click copy buttons.
  • Customizable Mod Settings: Directly configure hotkeys and color formatting preferences within the Windhawk UI.

Hotkey & Controls

  • Activate Eyedropper: Default hotkey is Win + Alt + C (customizable in Windhawk settings).
  • Pick Color: Left-Click anywhere on the screen to capture the pixel color and open the copy window.
  • Cancel Eyedropper: Press Escape or Right-Click to exit picking mode without selecting a color.

Configuration Settings

You can customize the mod settings directly from the Windhawk Mod Manager UI:

Setting Type Default Description
Hotkey Key String C Single alphabet character used with Win + Alt (selectable via a dropdown menu).
Include '#' Prefix in HEX Boolean true Choose whether HEX values include the # symbol (#CDCDCD vs CDCDCD).
Uppercase HEX Characters Boolean true Toggle uppercase vs. lowercase HEX characters (#ABCDEF vs #abcdef).

Dependencies & Technical Details

  • Target Process: windhawk.exe (runs as a Windhawk tool mod)
  • Libraries Linked: -lgdi32, -lmsimg32, -ldwmapi, -luxtheme, -lshcore
  • Architecture: Pure Win32 GDI & User32 APIs (no heavy external GUI dependencies).

entry.title: Confetti Spawner 1.4.0
entry.content:
Confetti Spawner

Press a hotkey and a burst of confetti (or color emoji) flies across the monitor under your mouse pointer. Hold the hotkey to keep it going. The effect is drawn on a click-through overlay that never takes focus, so you can keep typing and clicking while it plays.

The overlay only exists while particles are on screen. When the last particle is gone the window is destroyed and the frame timer stops, so the mod uses no CPU while idle.

The mod runs in its own small Windhawk process and does not inject into any other program.

Hotkeys

Default Action
Ctrl+Alt+F10 Fire a burst. Hold the keys to keep firing
none Cycle the origin (sides, top, bottom, cursor, random) and fire
none Cycle the mode (confetti, emoji, mixed) and fire

The cycle hotkeys are off by default. Set them in the settings to use them.

While the mod is enabled, its hotkey combinations are reserved system-wide, so other apps stop receiving them. Pick combinations you don't use elsewhere (for example Ctrl+Shift+C is copy in Windows Terminal). On keyboard layouts with AltGr, AltGr is sent as Ctrl+Alt, so a Ctrl+Alt+<letter> hotkey can block a character you type with AltGr. Function keys are a safe choice.

Hotkeys are written as modifiers plus a key, for example Ctrl+Alt+F10, Alt+F9, Ctrl+Shift+F9 or Ctrl+Alt+Space. Modifiers are Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Win. Keys can be a letter, a digit, F1 to F24, Space, Enter, Tab, Esc, Insert, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, the arrow keys (Up, Down, Left, Right), Num0 to Num9, Pause or PrintScreen. Type none (or leave the field empty) to turn a hotkey off. If another program already owns a combination, it can't be registered; the mod log says so.

Hold to fire: while the fire hotkey (its main key and modifiers) stays held, the mod keeps emitting at the normal rate (particle count per emission time) and stops when you let go. A quick tap still plays one full burst.

Cycling the origin or the mode only lasts until the settings are saved again or the mod restarts. The saved settings are not changed.

Modes

  • Confetti: paper pieces in the shapes and colors you pick. With Flip enabled they tumble in 3D as they fall.
  • Emoji: the emoji from the Emoji list, drawn in full color.
  • Mixed: both at once. Emoji share sets how many of the particles are emoji.

Origins

  • Sides: two cannons in the bottom corners shooting up and inward (the classic look). Side cannon angle sets how steeply they fire: 70 is classic, 90 shoots straight up, lower values shoot flatter toward the middle.
  • Top: confetti rain from the top edge.
  • Bottom: a fountain from the bottom center.
  • Cursor: an explosion from the mouse pointer. Every particle spawns at the pointer position at the moment it is emitted, so moving the mouse while holding the hotkey drags the stream along, even onto another monitor.
  • Random: one of the above, picked per burst.

Settings

The defaults reproduce the original classic confetti: sides origin, 600 rectangular pieces in six colors, no 3D flip, long lifetime.

Windhawk number settings are whole numbers, so decimal values are stored scaled. Each setting's description says how: for example Gravity is in hundredths, so 50 means 0.50, and Drag is in thousandths, so 990 means 0.990.

  • Particle count, Emission time, Speed, Gravity, Spread, Source width: shape of the burst. Emission time is how long a burst keeps spawning particles.
  • Wobble, Size, Spin, Drag: how particles move and look while falling. Drag is the share of velocity kept per 60 Hz tick.
  • Lifetime, Fade, Opacity: how long particles live, whether they fade out over the last quarter of their life, and the overall overlay opacity.
  • Frame rate: animation frame rate. Physics is time based, so the motion looks the same at any frame rate; higher is only smoother.
  • Emoji, Emoji size, Emoji spin: the emoji list is separated by spaces. Joined emoji sequences (such as family or flag emoji) are kept intact.
  • Shapes, Colors: confetti shapes (rect, square, circle, triangle, star, heart) and colors (#RRGGBB). Each list item can also hold several values separated by commas.
  • Preview on save: fire one burst whenever you save the settings, handy while tuning.

Tips

  • Bursts land on the monitor under the pointer and on the virtual desktop you are on.
  • Firing again while a burst is still playing on the same monitor adds to it.
  • Old overlays keep animating until empty after the pointer moves to another monitor.
  • For a snow look, use origin Top, shape circle, color #FFFFFF, gravity 5 and wobble 20.
  • Very high particle counts on 4K monitors cost more GPU and CPU time per frame. A single overlay is capped at 8000 live particles.

entry.title: macOS Gestures - Mission Control 1.3.1
entry.content:
macOS Gestures - Mission Control

Mission Control for Windows. A three-finger swipe up on a precision touchpad opens a live, animated overview of all your windows; the overview follows your fingers the whole way, and springs into place when you let go. Swipe back down, press Esc, or pick a window to leave.

What you get

  • Live window previews (the same technology the taskbar and Alt+Tab use, so videos keep playing) laid out in a clean grid, with the app icon and title under each window.
  • Minimized windows are shown too, and dialogs are drawn on top of the window they belong to.
  • The taskbar slides out of the screen with your fingers and comes back when you pick a window.
  • A virtual desktops bar flush with the bottom edge: see your desktops, switch to one or create a new one. It fades in with the swipe.
  • A close button on the window under the mouse (also the middle mouse button and the Delete key), with the remaining windows gliding to their new places.
  • Keyboard: Esc closes, arrow keys / Tab move the selection, Enter or Space picks it.
  • Spring physics with the finger speed carried over; pushing further up when everything is already open stretches the grid with rubber-band resistance.
  • Respects the Windows "Animation effects" setting, and is switched off over fullscreen apps and games.

Three-finger left / right

Windows only lets a program take over all three-finger swipes at once, so the mod performs the Alt+Tab itself: swipe right for Alt+Tab, left for Alt+Shift+Tab, and keep swiping to keep cycling. It can also be set to do nothing.

Requirements

  • Windows 11 with the touchpad gestures API (TouchpadGesturesController) and a precision touchpad. On builds without that API the mod stays idle and the log says "TouchpadGesturesController not supported".
  • The mod runs only in the shell's explorer.exe (not in folder windows opened in a separate process, nor in Explorer's COM helper processes).

What changes in Windows

  • While the mod runs it takes over all three-finger swipes, so Windows' own three-finger actions are off: swipe up (Task View) and swipe down (show desktop) have no Windows replacement while Mission Control is closed. Turning the mod off gives them back.
  • The left/right swipe sends Alt+Tab as keystrokes. When an app running as administrator has the focus, Windows blocks those keystrokes, so that swipe does nothing there. The desktops bar uses Windows' Win+Ctrl shortcuts the same way and has the same limit.

Conflicts

  • CoverTabby with its touchpad option turned on also takes over three-finger swipes. Use only one of the two for touchpad gestures.

Settings

Everything above can be changed from the Settings tab: background material (Mica, Mica Alt, Acrylic, live blur, blurred wallpaper), swipe distance, which parts to show, and the animation tuning (speed, bounce, stretch, background fade).

Notes

  • The live previews use private DWM functions, which Windows updates can change. If they stop working the mod falls back to the classic thumbnails on its own.
  • Other mods that animate windows closing (like Windows Animations) are kept from playing their animation in front of Mission Control: a window is hidden just before it is closed. Keep that mod's option to animate hidden windows turned off. If the window is still there a moment later (it asked "Save changes?", or it closes to the tray), it is shown again.
  • Mission Control shows up to 24 windows.
  • If the mod does not start at logon, turn on logging in the mod's Advanced tab in Windhawk and check the log output: the start-up steps are logged there.

entry.title: Taskbar Active Window Highlight 0.1.1
entry.content:
Taskbar Active Window Highlight

When an app has several windows, Windows 11's thumbnail preview gives no hint about which one is active. This mod adds an accent-colored highlight to the active window's card. The taskbar button keeps Windows' native indicator.

Requires the Windows 11 taskbar's XAML thumbnail previews (tested on Windows 11 build 26300). With the classic thumbnails, or with StartAllBack or ExplorerPatcher, the mod has no effect.

How it works

The mod does not track focus itself. It reads the state Explorer already keeps:

  • The taskbar's active task item (TaskbarAppsList.ActiveItem), which names the active window. The mod follows Explorer's own change notifications.
  • Each thumbnail card's view model, which names the window the card shows.

The highlight is a separate element placed right above the card's own background, below the title, icon and preview image. Its size and corner radius are bound to that background, so it follows themes such as Windows 11 Taskbar Styler.

Clicking the taskbar or a preview list briefly moves focus to the taskbar itself. By default the last active window stays highlighted until another window or the desktop takes focus, or the window is minimized or closed.

How it differs from Taskbar Recent Focus Highlight

Taskbar Recent Focus Highlight ranks apps and windows by recent use, from its own focus history. This mod answers a narrower question, which window is active right now, by reading Explorer's own active task item, with no focus tracking of its own. While another app has focus it marks nothing in this app's preview, and it also marks single-window previews.

Performance and footprint

  • Event-driven only. No background thread, timers, polling or focus tracking. The mod runs only when Explorer reports a new active window or binds a preview card to a window.
  • Nothing on hover or layout. Moving the mouse over the taskbar or previews runs no mod code.
  • Under 1 ms, usually about 0.01 ms. Measured in normal use: typical 0.004–0.013 ms per event, worst case 0.67 ms (the first time a card's highlight is created).
  • One element per card, created once and then only shown or hidden.
  • Safe to unload. No event handlers are left in Explorer, so disabling the mod cleanly removes it.

entry.title: 1 Letter Language Indicator 1.0
entry.content:
1 Letter Language Indicator

Simplifies the input language indicator in the Windows 11 taskbar tray to a single letter: ENG becomes E, and ENG (US) becomes E.

The indicator keeps updating when you switch input languages, and the original text is restored when the mod is disabled.

Settings

  • Letter size: the font size of the letter. Set it to 0 to keep the Windows size (12).
  • Letter color: separate colors for light mode and dark mode, chosen by the taskbar's theme (the Windows mode). Each one can be:
    • A hex color (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB) or a color name (Red, White).
    • accent for the Windows accent color, or one of its shades: accentLight1 to accentLight3, accentDark1 to accentDark3. The letter follows accent color changes.
    • Empty, to keep the Windows color in that mode.
  • Vertical offset: moves the letter up (negative) or down (positive), in pixels. Useful for re-centering the letter after changing its size.
  • Indicator width: the language indicator normally reserves room for three letters. With a single letter that leaves empty space, so by default the indicator is narrowed to 32 pixels, the width of a regular tray icon. Set it to 0 to keep the Windows width.

Notes

  • Languages and layouts which start with the same letter look the same, e.g. ENG (US) and ENG (UK), or ENG and ESP.
  • Other mods may set the same properties. "Taskbar tray icon spacing and grid" sets the width of the language indicator: while Indicator width is set, this mod's width wins. Windows 11 Taskbar Styler themes which change the font size or color of the indicator conflict with Letter size and Letter color, and whichever mod applies last wins. To let the other mod control a property, set the matching setting to 0 (or leave the color empty).

Target

SystemTray.LanguageTextIconContent > Grid#ContainerGrid >
SystemTray.AdaptiveTextBlock#LanguageInnerTextBlock > TextBlock#InnerTextBlock

Only Windows 11 is supported.

entry.title: Explorer Item Pins 1.1.5
entry.content:
Explorer Item Pins

English · Русский

Explorer Item Pins keeps selected files and folders at the top of their parent folder in Windows File Explorer. Each folder has its own pins.

Features
  • Two ways to pin. Use the modern context menu or the pin button between Share and Delete on the command bar.
  • Sort and group. Pins stay at the top in either sort direction. With grouping on, they appear in the first group, Pinned. Explorer's sorting still applies within the group.
  • Pin indicator. A pushpin appears at the upper-right corner of the file or folder icon. It follows the icon size and works with thumbnails, lists, details, tiles and content view.
  • Interface languages. English, Russian, Spanish, German, Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified Chinese.

Platforms

Requires Windows 11 x64 or ARM64 with the tabbed File Explorer.

Data exchange

Pins are stored separately for each Windows account. Uninstalling the mod removes its pins. Replacing a file under the same name keeps its pin. A rename within the same folder can keep the pin when the mod can identify the original file. Copying or moving an item to another folder does not carry its pin with it.

Usage

  1. Select a file or folder and choose Pin in item pane in its context menu, or click the pin on the command bar.
  2. To remove the pin, select the item and choose Unpin from item pane or click the crossed-out pin on the command bar. The item returns to its usual position in the folder.

In Windhawk, open the mod's Settings to control these options independently. All three are enabled by default.

If the pin commands are missing from a File Explorer window that was already open when the mod was enabled or updated, reopen that window.

Setting Controls
Context menu command Pin and unpin in the context menu
Command bar button Pin and unpin on the File Explorer command bar
Pinned item indicator The pushpin on pinned file and folder icons

Links

  • Explorer Item Pins on GitHub
  • DSN Windhawk Mods

entry.title: Notepad++ Dark Dialog Fix 1.0.3
entry.content:
Notepad++ Dark Dialog Fix

In dark mode, Notepad++ paints its Save and confirm dialogs dark but leaves the text black, so you can barely read it. This mod makes that text light again.

Features

  • Readable dialog text in Save, Save changes and other confirm dialogs.
  • Fixes labels and buttons drawn with the theme's text color.
  • Only in dark mode. The mod asks Notepad++ whether dark mode is on, so light mode dialogs are left alone. Needs Notepad++ 8.4.1 or newer.
  • Only touches Notepad++. No other app is affected, and nothing is changed on disk.

entry.title: Compact RDP connection bar 3.0.0
entry.content:
Compact RDP connection bar

Shrinks the top connection bar of Remote Desktop Connection (Ctrl+Alt+Home).

The bar normally spans a large fixed width: a small button group on the left, the hostname in the middle, the window buttons on the right. This mod keeps the hostname zone, keeps the button groups, and drops the empty space between them.

Works with any number of toolbars. A toolbar whose buttons are all hidden needs no width and is simply not given any, which is what happens once the pin and quality buttons are hidden.

The right toolbar carries the window buttons - minimize, restore and close. Each can be hidden separately; hide all three and the bar shrinks to the hostname alone. A single remaining toolbar keeps the side it originally sat on, so hiding the window buttons does not move the pin group to the right.

The quality indicator is a lock icon that mstsc only shows in some sessions. Ticking the setting when it is absent changes nothing, and the bar is laid out exactly as it would be without the setting.

Screenshots

Before After After2 After3 After4

Settings

  • Text area width - target width of the hostname zone, scaled for DPI. Raised automatically when the hostname needs more room.
  • Hide pin button - hides the pin (keep on top) button.
  • Hide quality button - hides the connection quality indicator.
  • Hide lock button - hides the lock icon mstsc shows next to the quality indicator. The button is only present in some sessions; when it is absent, nothing changes.
  • Hide minimize / restore / close - hide the window buttons on the right. Hiding the close button removes the only visible way to disconnect; the session can still be closed from the taskbar icon, or Ctrl+Alt+Break leaves full screen so the bar and the window controls come back.

entry.title: Chrome clear on exit with keep sites 0.4.1
entry.content:
Chrome clear on exit with keep sites

Clear Chrome's browsing data when its last window closes normally, while keeping login cookies and ordinary site storage for domains you choose. Chrome performs the deletion. The mod supplies its settings through Chrome's native policy reader.

Cleanup is off by default. Review the keep list, then turn on Enable automatic cleanup in the mod's Settings tab. The list starts empty: enabling cleanup with no exceptions signs you out of most websites. Deleted data cannot be recovered. Enter domains such as example.com; subdomains are included. Full HTTP/HTTPS URLs are accepted, with their paths and ports ignored. Use ASCII/punycode domain names.

Check your configuration

Restart Chrome after installing the mod. At chrome://policy, select Reload policies and check these three entries:

  • ClearBrowsingDataOnExitList: browsing history, download history, cached images and files, autofill, site settings, and hosted-app data, for all time.
  • DefaultCookiesSetting: 4, making ordinary site storage session-only.
  • CookiesAllowedForUrls: your keep list, preserving cookies and ordinary storage.

The keep list does not preserve history, cache, permissions, or legacy hosted-app storage. Downloaded files, bookmarks, and saved passwords are not selected for deletion. Websites can still expire their own sessions or require a new login.

Chrome already exposes the cookie/storage controls at chrome://settings/content/siteData. This mod sets those controls and their Allowed to save data on your device exceptions from one Windhawk keep list, and adds the broader exit cleanup policy which has no equivalent Chrome setting. Another clearing extension or an existing Chrome cleanup rule can still remove the data you intended to keep.

Changes and removal

After changing settings, use Reload policies to verify the result. The mod also requests a refresh when it has observed Chrome registering its policy events. Chrome processes these requests asynchronously; the mod cannot acknowledge when Chrome has finished applying them.

To stop cleanup, turn the setting off or disable the mod, then Reload policies before closing Chrome and confirm that the supplied entries have disappeared. Chrome can otherwise retain its cached policies for the remainder of that session. The next Chrome start with the mod disabled receives no policies from this mod. No administrator prompt, PowerShell helper, or policy-removal permission is needed.

The mod runs only in Chrome's browser process and does not change its real policy registry keys or profile files. It uses private temporary storage within Windhawk's mod storage while cleanup is enabled. Inactive files can remain after Chrome exits; a later enabled start attempts to remove verified leftovers when they are no longer in use. These files are never reused as configuration or needed for backup.

Scope and limitations

  • Applies to all profiles in each Chrome browser process that loads the mod. Chrome must be allowed to load Windhawk mods.
  • Intended for personal installations. Conflicting existing local Chrome policies prevent injection; they are never replaced. Chrome's normal cloud-policy precedence still applies. Check Windhawk's mod log if the entries do not appear.
  • If a policy view cannot be prepared, Chrome uses its genuine policies for that load. The mod logs the reason; check the policy page to confirm cleanup is active. If private storage could not be initialized, save the mod's settings again to retry. Once storage is ready, reloading Chrome policies retries a failed read.
  • Chrome can show Managed by your organization while these policies are active. Chrome also disables synchronization of affected data categories.
  • Normal last-window close is the supported cleanup path. Crashes, forced termination, Windows shutdown, and some restart/quit paths can prevent completion or defer selective site-data deletion until the next start.
  • Disabling the mod cannot restore browsing data Chrome has already deleted.

Back up the source and your Windhawk settings to reproduce the configuration on a fresh Windows installation. The source's defaults do not contain your saved list.

References

  • Chrome exit cleanup policy
  • Chromium Windows policy loader
  • Chromium registry policy conversion
  • Windows application hives

entry.title: Disable Web Search in Start Menu 1.0.0
entry.content:
Disable Web Search in Start Menu

The search UI that the Start menu and the taskbar open mixes results from Bing into local results. Windows can be told to stop doing that with settings and policies, but they are read when the search UI starts, so changing them means signing out, and the registry entries stay behind afterwards.

This mod does the same thing without touching the registry. It sits in the search UI process and answers the setting reads as if web search had been turned off. Turning the mod off gives the old behavior back the next time the search UI starts.

On both Windows 10 and Windows 11, typing in the Start menu hands the query to this search UI, so the Start menu search is covered as well.

Settings

  • Also hide cloud content results reports the two "Cloud content search" switches from Settings as off. The Windows 11 search UI asks for them before it puts web results in the list, so turning this setting off can bring web results back, and leaving it on also removes OneDrive, Outlook and SharePoint results from search.

Notes

  • Nothing is written to the registry and no files are touched. The values the mod reports are the ones Windows itself uses:
    • DisableSearchBoxSuggestions, ConnectedSearchUseWeb and DisableWebSearch, the web search policies
    • BingSearchEnabled, the older web results switch
    • IsMSACloudSearchEnabled, IsAADCloudSearchEnabled and AllowCloudSearch, the cloud content switches, only with the setting above If you set any of these yourself, the mod simply agrees.
  • The search UI is a packaged app and reaches the registry through the API sets, which end up in kernelbase.dll. Desktop callers import advapi32.dll, whose exports are separate entry points rather than forwarders on current builds. Both are hooked, so neither path is missed.
  • Web results are decided while the search UI sets up, so after enabling the mod or changing a setting, end SearchHost.exe in Task Manager. Windows starts it again on the next search, and the new settings are read then.
  • If web results survive, turn on the mod's log and open the search UI once. The log lists every read the mod answered, which shows whether the process asks for these values at all.

entry.title: Dynamic Island Media Player 1.6.0
entry.content:
Dynamic Island Media Player for Windows

A focused, customizable Dynamic Island overlay for Windows that becomes an interactive media player when music or video is playing. Based on the original Dynamic Island for Windows, this standalone mod removes unrelated dashboard modules and concentrates on media playback.

Key Features

  • Media integration: Track title, artist, album, source-app badge, album artwork, playback state, and progress information through Windows System Media Transport Controls. Artwork is refreshed when metadata settles, stale provider thumbnails are rechecked briefly, and large covers are downscaled to reduce memory use.
  • Playback controls: Play/pause, previous/next track, and progress scrubbing.
  • Track transitions: Choose between crossfade (Fade) and horizontal slide animations. Track transitions work independently from the option that disables the island's hover and movement animations.
  • Interactive island: Expand on hover, click-through mode with Ctrl-to-interact, and configurable show/hide, next, previous, and play/pause hotkeys.
  • Window behavior: Always-on-top, above-games behavior, taskbar layering, fullscreen handling, and per-application saved positions.
  • Context menu: Right-click configuration with color and opacity dialogs, playback-related options, and persistent menu overrides.
  • Color customization: Theme presets, background/text colors, automatic/system/custom accent colors, and a user-managed color-morphing palette with speed controls.
  • Appearance: Multiple island shapes, adjustable size and text scale, custom font, button styles, shadow toggle, and monitor selection.
  • Localization: Ukrainian, Russian, and English interface languages.
  • Media source filtering: Optionally restrict the player to the currently selected media source.

Credits

  • Himanshu (devcode90): Original Dynamic Island for Windows framework, rendering foundation, and core interface design.
  • BOG090909: Standalone media-player adaptation, per-app positioning, customization features, localization, playback integration, and performance improvements.

entry.title: New Windows Search Extensions 0.1.0
entry.content:
Updated for Build 26320.9876 (Windows 11 Insider Beta). Insider builds change quickly, so newer builds may break or move this.

New Windows Search Extensions

This is only for the NEW Windows search: the compact "composer" search box on recent Windows 11 Insider builds (hosted by shellhost.exe loadComponent SystemComposerControl, the one with inline actions like "Turn on dark mode" and the volume slider). It does nothing for the classic Start menu search, the old taskbar search flyout (SearchHost.exe) or Windows 10.

Adds new kinds of results to the new search box, mixed in with the native ones:

  • Calculator: type 12*7.5, (3+4)^2, sqrt(2), 200 * 15%, 50 + 10% and press Enter to copy the result. Supports + - * / ^ %, brackets, pi, e and sqrt cbrt abs sin cos tan asin acos atan ln log log2 exp round floor ceil.
  • Unit converter: 5 km in mi, 72 f to c, 1.5 gb in mb, 3 cups to ml. Length, weight, volume, time, speed, data size and temperature.
  • Kill process: kill note lists the running processes whose name contains "note", with their memory use; Enter ends the selected one. It's ended at once, like "End task" in Task Manager, so unsaved work in it is lost. Only processes you're allowed to end are listed.
  • Custom commands: your own keywords, set in the mod settings. A keyword can open a program, file, folder or URL. Put {query} in the command to pass on what you type after the keyword: with the default g command, g windhawk searches Google for "windhawk". Such a command shows up once you've typed something after the keyword.

Each one can be turned off in the settings.

For developers: add your own results

Other mods, and any program or script, can put items into the new search box through this mod. Providers see every query and decide for themselves when to answer, so no prefix is needed. The Demo provider setting adds sample items (type wh hello: an echo/copy item, a toggle, a "run" item and a card).

Above: examples/weather_client.py, an out-of-process provider talking over the named pipe.

Items are injected as genuine native search providers. Windows' own search is built from Palette extensions (Windows.UI.Palettes): Apps, Files, Settings, Windows Actions, Command Line and so on are each one extension. This mod adds one more extension per provider (the built-in ones included), so the items are real PaletteItems. They mix into the native list with native ranking, keyboard navigation, icons, toggles and Adaptive Card content.

Two ways to provide items

1. From another Windhawk mod (in-process)

Your mod must also @include shellhost.exe. Find this mod's DLL and call its exported C API (Windhawk exports every symbol of a mod DLL):

typedef struct WSE_ProviderCallbacks {
    UINT32 cbSize;
    void* ctx;
    // Called for every query (text may be empty = zero state). Answer with
    // WSE_SubmitResults(queryHandle, itemsJson, done) from any thread, now or later.
    void (WINAPI* onQuery)(void* ctx, UINT64 queryHandle, PCWSTR text, PCWSTR queryJson);
    // An item was invoked: actionId is "invoke", "toggle" or a card action id.
    void (WINAPI* onInvoke)(void* ctx, PCWSTR itemId, PCWSTR actionId, PCWSTR dataJson, PCWSTR inputsJson);
    // Optional. Query abandoned (user typed more / closed search).
    void (WINAPI* onCancel)(void* ctx, UINT64 queryHandle);
    // Optional. The library is unloading: drop the provider handle, don't call the API again.
    void (WINAPI* onDetach)(void* ctx);
} WSE_ProviderCallbacks;

int    WINAPI WSE_GetApiVersion(void);                                   // 1
UINT64 WINAPI WSE_RegisterProvider(PCWSTR providerJson, const WSE_ProviderCallbacks* cb);
BOOL   WINAPI WSE_SubmitResults(UINT64 queryHandle, PCWSTR itemsJson, BOOL done);
BOOL   WINAPI WSE_SetStaticItems(UINT64 provider, PCWSTR itemsJson);     // items always offered (GetItems)
BOOL   WINAPI WSE_UpdateCard(UINT64 provider, PCWSTR itemId, PCWSTR dataJson); // live-update a card's data
BOOL   WINAPI WSE_NotifyChanged(UINT64 provider);                        // ask search to re-query
BOOL   WINAPI WSE_UnregisterProvider(UINT64 provider);                   // waits for running callbacks

Finding the library: enumerate the modules of the process and use the first one that exports WSE_GetApiVersion. Mods load in any order, so retry for a few seconds if it isn't there yet (and again later: the library can be disabled, updated or re-enabled while your mod is running; onDetach tells you it's going).

Callbacks run on the library's worker threads, never on Windows' own threads. Call WSE_UnregisterProvider in your Wh_ModUninit: it returns once none of your callbacks is running any more, so your DLL can unload safely. (Calling it from inside one of your own callbacks is fine too; it then waits for the others.)

2. From any process (named pipe)

Connect to \\.\pipe\WindhawkSearchExtensions-<session id> (the Windows session id of your process, e.g. ProcessIdToSessionId) and exchange newline-delimited UTF-8 JSON messages. Each connection can register any number of providers. They're removed automatically when the connection closes.

Only processes running as the same user can open the pipe. Any of them can register a provider, and a provider sees the text typed into search. That's why the Named pipe API setting is off by default: turn it on to use the pipe.

Client to library:

{"op":"register","provider":{"id":"weather","name":"Weather","glyph":"\uE706"}}
{"op":"results","queryId":"17","items":[ ... ],"done":true}
{"op":"setItems","provider":"weather","items":[ ... ]}
{"op":"updateCard","provider":"weather","itemId":"now","data":{ ... }}
{"op":"refresh","provider":"weather"}
{"op":"unregister","provider":"weather"}

Library to client:

{"op":"registered","provider":"weather","extensionId":"Windhawk.weather"}
{"op":"query","provider":"weather","queryId":"17","text":"weather lond","query":{...}}
{"op":"cancel","provider":"weather","queryId":"17"}
{"op":"invoke","provider":"weather","itemId":"now","actionId":"invoke","data":"","inputs":""}
{"op":"error","message":"..."}

Provider JSON

{
  "id": "weather",                       // unique, [A-Za-z0-9._-]
  "name": "Weather",                     // shown in search settings/diagnostics
  "description": "Current conditions",
  "glyph": "\uE706", "font": "Segoe Fluent Icons",  // or "icon": "C:\\path\\icon.png"
  "zeroState": false,                    // also asked when the box is empty
  "kinds": ["QueryResult.SystemComposer"],          // advanced: palette kinds this source serves
  "itemKinds": ["Command"]               // default kinds for items
}

Item JSON

{
  "id": "now",                           // stable id within the provider
  "title": "London: 14°C, light rain",
  "subtitle": "Feels like 12°C",         // string or array of strings
  "icon": {"glyph": "\uE9E2", "font": "Segoe Fluent Icons"},  // or {"uri": "https://..."} / {"path": "C:\\x.png"} / "C:\\x.png"
  "tags": [{"text": "Live", "tooltip": "Updated just now"}],
  "kinds": ["Command"],
  "score": 0.9,                          // goes to the native ranking (KnownPaletteProperties.Score)
  "properties": {"Path": "C:\\Users"},   // any extra KnownPaletteProperties
  "action": {"type": "callback"},        // default: onInvoke(id, "invoke")
  //  {"type":"uri","uri":"https://bbc.co.uk/weather"}
  //  {"type":"run","command":"notepad.exe","args":"x.txt"}
  //  {"type":"copy","text":"14°C"}
  //  {"type":"toggle","isToggled":true}   -> onInvoke(id, "toggle", "true"|"false")
  "card": {                              // optional Adaptive Card content (template + data)
    "template": { "type": "AdaptiveCard", "version": "1.5", "body": [ ... ], "actions": [ ... ] },
    "data": { ... }                      // Action.Submit/Execute -> onInvoke(id, actionId, data, inputs)
  }
}

Notes

  • This mod only works on builds that have the new composer search (Windows.UI.Palettes). Elsewhere it does nothing.
  • Windows reads its provider list once, when the composer starts. If the mod is enabled while the composer is already running, it restarts the composer (setting Restart search when enabled late). The composer comes back the next time you open search. Providers registered later (other mods, pipe clients) are picked up live.
  • When the mod is disabled or updated, Windows may still hold some of its objects (items it's showing, finished queries). The mod then restarts the composer instead of unloading under them; search reopens normally next time.
  • Card buttons: cards render under the selected row and you can update them live (WSE_UpdateCard / updateCard). But Windows ignores Action.Submit buttons in that inline preview ("slot previews do not support card actions"). Put the action on the item itself.
  • Pipe clients: if you open the pipe as an ordinary synchronous handle (Python open(), .NET FileStream without async), don't write from one thread while another is blocked reading. Windows serializes I/O on synchronous handles and the write waits forever. Either answer from the reading thread or open the pipe overlapped.
  • Enable logging for the mod in Windhawk to see the queries and what Windows asks of the providers.

entry.title: Adaptive Windows 1.0.0
entry.content:
Adaptive Windows

(Português do Brasil logo abaixo / Brazilian Portuguese below)

English

An automatic tiling window manager for Windows 11, inspired by the Nava OS concept videos and by four tools: tacky-borders (focus border), komorebi (tiling), AltSnap (moving and resizing windows with Alt + mouse) and Loop (radial menu). Here you get all of it in one place. It arranges the windows of each monitor in a grid, animates every change with fluid transitions, and works together with minimize / restore / open animation mods: a window is animated straight to the new place assigned by the grid, not to where it used to be.

The mod runs in its own windhawk.exe process (a Windhawk "tool mod"), not inside Explorer, so a problem in it cannot take down the taskbar or File Explorer.

Features

  • Automatic grid. A new window takes a slot and the others make room for it; when a window closes or is minimized, the rest take over the free space.
  • Respects each app's minimum size. The grid reshapes itself so no window ends up smaller than its app allows or overlaps another one (for example Outlook and Spotify together on a short screen). If a chosen layout does not fit, the automatic layout is used.
  • Free resizing. Drag a window edge and the grid adapts to the width or height you chose: the other windows give way while you drag. Dragging a window by its title and dropping it over another one swaps the two; dropping it anywhere else sends it back to its slot.
  • Move windows with the keyboard. Win + Alt + arrows swap the focused window with its neighbor on that side.
  • Move windows with the mouse (radial menu, optional). Hold the right button (or another one you choose) over a window and a ring appears at the cursor. Move the mouse towards a side: the slot of the neighbor on that side is highlighted. Release and the two windows swap places.
  • Maximized windows that return to or enter the grid go back to normal mode and take their slot. Turn on Keep maximized windows maximized to leave them alone instead: they stay maximized, outside the grid, and take their slot again when they stop being maximized. A maximized window never gets the drawn border, and the drawn border and its glow are clipped to the window's monitor, so they do not spill onto the monitor next to it.
  • Animated border on the focused window: color, effect (solid, pulse, rainbow, gradient), line width, glow, corner radius and offset, so it can match your rounded corners mod.
  • Multiple monitors. Each monitor has its own grid, and windows can be dragged between them, including monitors with different display scales. It works within the limits each window or app imposes: the minimum size is decided by the app (and grows with the monitor's scale), so an app whose minimum is wider than the monitor will overflow its right / bottom edge.
  • Display scale aware. The gap, the screen-edge margin and the border sizes (width, glow, offset, corner radius) are set in pixels at 100% scale and scaled for each monitor, so they look the same on a 100% and on a 200% monitor.
  • Virtual desktops. When you switch desktops, the windows of the desktop you come back to return to the same slots and order, without replaying the entrance animation.

Free resizing: when it works

Dragging a window border adapts the grid only when all of these are true:

  • The window is in the grid: not taken out with the float hotkey, not maximized and not minimized.
  • There are at least two windows in the grid on the same monitor.
  • You drag an edge that faces another window. An edge against the screen border has no neighbor to take space from, so dragging it does nothing and the window goes back to its slot.
  • You hold the window by its border (within about 12 px of the left, right or bottom edge, or the top 5 px) and change its size by more than 6 px. Holding it by the middle or the title bar moves the window instead (drop it over another window to swap, anywhere else to send it back).

You do not have to aim at the border: with Resize a window with Alt + right button on, hold Alt and the right button anywhere over the window and drag sideways or up/down. The side nearest to the cursor follows the mouse (the right side if you hold the right half of the window, and so on): drag outward to enlarge the window, inward to shrink it. The other windows move out of the way while you drag, so nothing overlaps. A side against the screen border has no neighbor, so the opposite side is used instead; if neither side has a neighbor, the window goes back to its slot. Esc cancels.

Windows can be moved in a similar way: turn on Move windows with Alt + left button, hold Alt and the left button anywhere over a window, and drag. A floating window just moves. A window of the grid is pulled out of the grid after a short drag (about 40 px) and follows the mouse as a floating window. If the radial menu is set to Alt + left button, that gesture opens the menu over windows of the grid instead.

If you also use AltDrag or AltSnap. They use the same two gestures (Alt + left button to move, Alt + right button to resize) on every window. With both running, a drag over a window this mod manages goes to this mod, and a drag anywhere else goes to them. To avoid two tools answering the same gesture, leave these two options off here (they are off by default) or change the gesture there.

In the "main left" / "main top" layouts, dragging the divider of the main window changes how much of the screen it takes. Each app's minimum size still applies. Your sizes are discarded when a window is opened, closed or minimized, when the layout changes and when you re-arrange everything (Win + Alt + Home).

Hotkeys

Hotkey Action
Win + Ctrl + G Cycle the layout: auto, columns, rows, grid, main left, main top
Win + Ctrl + T Take the focused window out of the grid (it stays where it is and the others use the space); press again to put it back
Win + Alt + F Focus mode: every window on the monitor fills the screen; press again to leave
Win + Alt + ← / → Move the focused window left / right: swaps it with the window next to it on that side, whatever the layout (does nothing if there is none)
Win + Alt + ↑ / ↓ Move the focused window up / down: swaps it with the window directly above / below it (does nothing if there is none)
Win + Alt + Home Re-arrange everything and put all windows back in the grid

Every hotkey can be changed in the settings, and the change applies as soon as you save them:

  • Layout, float and re-arrange have their own text fields (for example Ctrl+Alt+G, Win+T or Alt+Home). Write modifiers (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win) and one key: a letter, a digit, or Up, Down, Left, Right, Home or End. Leave a field empty to turn that hotkey off.
  • Focus mode and the four arrows share one modifier choice: Win+Alt (default), Ctrl+Alt, Ctrl+Alt+Shift or Alt+Shift.
  • Avoid combinations without Win or Ctrl: they take the key away from every other app.

Hotkeys that cannot be registered are reported in the Windhawk log (error 1409 = already in use). Win + Alt + ↑ is one of them unless you turn on Take over hotkeys (see below). Win + Ctrl + T is also the default Always On Top shortcut of PowerToys: if you use both, change one of them.

Taking over shortcuts that are already in use

Windows itself uses some of these combinations: Win + Alt + ↑ snaps the window to the top half of the screen, so with the default settings it is unavailable to the mod (the log reports error 1409) and Windows keeps handling it. The mod never overrides another program's shortcut unless you ask it to. To use Win + Alt + ↑, turn on the Take over hotkeys option (off by default) or pick another set of modifiers for the arrows. With the option on, whenever a hotkey is already taken the mod catches that combination with a low-level keyboard hook, so the other program or Windows no longer receives it. The hook runs in a thread of its own, exists only while the mod runs, and only for the combinations that were already taken.

Radial menu: moving a window with the mouse

Off by default. In the settings, choose which button opens it: the right button, the middle button, or Alt / Win + the left button. Then press and hold that button over a window of the grid. A ring appears where the cursor is (after a brief hold, so a quick click does not flash it). Move the mouse out of the ring to the left, right, up or down: that slice of the ring lights up and the slot the window will go to is highlighted. Release the button to swap the window with the one in that slot. Esc cancels. If there is no window on that side, the slice turns gray and nothing happens. It only considers windows on the same monitor.

The center of the ring floats and un-floats windows without the keyboard. Keep the button pressed with the cursor still: a small circle in the middle fills up in about half a second. Release once it is full and the window leaves the grid (the others take its place). Do the same over a floating window and it goes back into the grid. Releasing before it is full is an ordinary click.

The ring has three themes: Liquid glass, the default (clear glass: the screen shows through sharp and bends at the edges of the ring), Glass (a frosted glass tube showing the blurred screen behind it) and Classic (a flat ring). The selection color paints the chosen slice and the highlight over the window that will receive the one you are moving. By default the colors are the focused window border ones, following its effect (pulse, rainbow, gradient); choose Custom to set the ring color and the selection color yourself. The ring thickness can be set too.

If you release without leaving the ring, the click is passed on to the app when the button is released, so a plain right click still opens the context menu. Over a window the mod manages (in the grid or floating), dragging with that button no longer works while the option is on; anywhere else (the desktop, the taskbar, maximized windows, ignored apps) the click is not touched at all. It needs a low-level mouse hook, which only exists while this option (or one of the two Alt gestures, resize or move) is on.

Works with other animation mods

Adaptive Windows works together with these two mods:

  • MacOS Minimize Animation (genie effect for minimize, restore and open).

  • Windows Animations.

Those mods hide the window and play their own animation. With the sync with open/close animations option on, Adaptive Windows notices this, puts the window in its final slot while it is hidden, and only animates the other windows making room, at the same time. Each window has a single animation, so nothing fights.

For the genie to land in the right place, while a window is minimized the mod writes into Windows the slot it will occupy when it comes back, and keeps that value up to date as the grid changes. This way the restore animation ends where the window will really be.

Programs you exclude in the other mod (for example Word in the genie mod) are not animated by it; in that case Adaptive Windows uses its own entrance animation.

Animations

The Nava OS style is the base (strong ease-out curve, new windows slide in from the right). There are also Smooth (slides in from the top), Snappy (no entrance effect) and Playful (enters from the bottom with a slight overshoot). While moving, a window keeps a fixed size (like when dragging): shrinking windows shrink at the start and growing ones only grow at the end, so nothing overlaps. The frame rate can follow the DWM (recommended), follow the highest refresh rate among your monitors, or be fixed (30 to 240 Hz).

Taskbar and dock

The usable area is the Windows work area. The screen-edge margin applies to all four sides. If the taskbar is hidden, windows only respect the screen edge. The bottom spacing setting (0 = automatic) is meant for docks drawn by another mod: enter the distance from the screen edge to the top of the dock. The taskbar can be on any edge of any monitor: the grid follows the Windows work area, and is re-computed when a monitor is connected or removed, the resolution changes, or the taskbar is moved or toggles auto-hide.

Corners

Uses the Windows 11 corner preference (default, rounded, small, square). Windows does not allow an arbitrary radius this way. If you already use a corner mod (for example "Custom Window Corner Radius"), leave this option on "do not touch" so the two do not fight over the corners.

Ignored windows and limits

  • Settings apply as soon as you save them; there is no need to restart the mod. Changing the apps that always stay out of the grid list also takes windows out of the grid (or brings them in) right away.
  • To take one window out of the grid for now, use the float hotkey (Win + Ctrl + T). To keep an app out of the grid always, write its name in that list (for example spotify;chrome). A name works if it is the program's name or if it appears in the window title. The list is empty by default.
  • Tool windows, always-on-top, non-focusable and non-resizable windows (panels, widgets) always stay out of the grid. The Windhawk log says why each window was ignored.
  • Windows that refuse to be positioned (a likely case is programs running as administrator) float after a few attempts; Win + Alt + Home tries again.
  • Moving windows with the keyboard only considers windows on the same monitor.

Português (Brasil)

Gerenciador de janelas em grade automática para o Windows 11, inspirado nos vídeos de conceito do Nava OS e em quatro ferramentas: tacky-borders (borda na janela em foco), komorebi (grade de janelas), AltSnap (mover e redimensionar janelas com Alt + mouse) e Loop (menu radial). Aqui você tem tudo isso em um único lugar. Ele organiza as janelas de cada monitor, anima as mudanças com transições fluidas e funciona junto com os mods de animação de minimizar, restaurar e abrir janelas: a janela é animada já para o novo lugar definido pela grade, e não para onde ela estava antes.

O mod roda em um processo windhawk.exe próprio (um "tool mod" do Windhawk), e não dentro do Explorer, então um problema nele não derruba a barra de tarefas nem o Explorador de Arquivos.

O que ele faz

  • Grade automática. Cada janela nova ocupa um espaço da grade e as outras abrem espaço para ela; ao fechar ou minimizar uma janela, as demais ocupam o espaço livre.
  • Respeita o tamanho mínimo de cada app. O formato da grade se ajusta sozinho para que nenhuma janela fique menor do que o app aceita nem sobreponha outra (por exemplo, Outlook e Spotify juntos numa tela de pouca altura). Se um layout escolhido não couber, ele usa o automático.
  • Redimensionamento livre. Arraste a borda de uma janela e a grade se adapta à largura ou à altura que você escolheu: as outras janelas abrem espaço enquanto você arrasta. Arrastar uma janela pelo meio e soltá-la sobre outra troca as duas de lugar; soltá-la em qualquer outro ponto a devolve ao seu espaço.
  • Mover janelas pelo teclado. Win + Alt + setas trocam a janela em foco com a vizinha daquele lado.
  • Mover janelas com o mouse (menu radial, opcional). Segure o botão direito (ou outro que você escolher) sobre uma janela e um anel aparece no cursor. Mova o mouse para um lado: o espaço da vizinha daquele lado é destacado. Solte e as duas janelas trocam de lugar.
  • Janelas maximizadas que voltam ou entram na grade passam ao modo normal e assumem o espaço. Ligue Manter janelas maximizadas para deixá-las em paz: elas continuam maximizadas, fora da grade, e assumem o espaço de novo quando deixam de estar maximizadas. Uma janela maximizada nunca recebe a borda desenhada, e a borda desenhada e o brilho são recortados no monitor da janela, para não passarem para o monitor ao lado.
  • Borda animada na janela em foco: cor, efeito (fixa, pulsar, arco-íris, degradê), largura da linha, brilho, raio dos cantos e deslocamento, para alinhar com o seu mod de cantos arredondados.
  • Vários monitores. Cada monitor tem a sua própria grade, e as janelas podem ser arrastadas entre eles, inclusive entre monitores de escalas diferentes. Funciona dentro dos limites impostos por cada janela ou app: o tamanho mínimo é decidido pelo app (e cresce com a escala do monitor), então um app cujo mínimo é maior que a largura do monitor vai passar da borda direita / de baixo.
  • Respeita a escala de cada monitor. O espaço entre janelas, a margem da borda da tela e as medidas da borda (largura, brilho, deslocamento, raio dos cantos) são configurados em pixels a 100% de escala e ajustados a cada monitor, então ficam iguais num monitor de 100% e num de 200%.
  • Áreas de trabalho virtuais. Ao trocar de área, as janelas da área para a qual você volta retomam os mesmos espaços e a mesma ordem, sem repetir a animação de entrada.

Redimensionamento livre: quando funciona

Arrastar a borda de uma janela adapta a grade apenas quando todas estas condições são verdadeiras:

  • A janela está na grade: não foi tirada com o atalho de soltar, nem está maximizada ou minimizada.
  • Há pelo menos duas janelas na grade no mesmo monitor.
  • Você arrasta uma borda que encosta em outra janela. Uma borda junto da borda da tela não tem vizinha para ceder espaço, então arrastá-la não faz nada e a janela volta ao seu espaço.
  • Você segura a janela pela borda (a cerca de 12 px da lateral esquerda, direita ou de baixo, ou nos 5 px de cima) e muda o tamanho em mais de 6 px. Segurar pelo meio ou pela barra de título move a janela (solte sobre outra para trocar, ou em qualquer outro ponto para devolvê-la).

Não é preciso mirar na borda: com Redimensionar a janela com Alt + botão direito ligado, segure Alt e o botão direito em qualquer ponto da janela e arraste para os lados ou para cima/baixo. A lateral mais próxima do cursor acompanha o mouse (a direita, se você segurar a metade direita da janela, e assim por diante): arraste para fora para aumentar a janela, para dentro para diminuir. As outras janelas abrem espaço enquanto você arrasta, sem sobreposição. Uma lateral junto da borda da tela não tem vizinha, então vale a lateral oposta; se nenhuma das duas tiver vizinha, a janela volta ao seu espaço. Esc cancela.

As janelas podem ser movidas de forma parecida: ligue Mover janelas com Alt + botão esquerdo, segure Alt e o botão esquerdo em qualquer ponto de uma janela e arraste. Uma janela solta apenas se move. Uma janela da grade é arrancada da grade depois de um arrasto curto (uns 40 px) e acompanha o mouse como janela solta. Se o menu radial estiver em Alt + botão esquerdo, esse gesto abre o menu sobre as janelas da grade.

Se você também usa o AltDrag ou o AltSnap. Eles usam os mesmos dois gestos (Alt + botão esquerdo para mover, Alt + botão direito para redimensionar) em qualquer janela. Com os dois ligados, um arrasto sobre uma janela que este mod administra fica com este mod, e em qualquer outro lugar fica com eles. Para não ter duas ferramentas respondendo ao mesmo gesto, deixe estas duas opções desligadas aqui (é o padrão) ou troque o gesto lá.

Nos layouts "principal à esquerda" / "principal em cima", arrastar a divisória da janela principal muda a parte da tela que ela ocupa. O tamanho mínimo de cada app continua valendo. Os tamanhos escolhidos são descartados quando uma janela é aberta, fechada ou minimizada, quando o layout muda e quando você reorganiza tudo (Win + Alt + Home).

Atalhos

Atalho Ação
Win + Ctrl + G Troca o layout: automático, colunas, linhas, grade, principal à esquerda, principal em cima
Win + Ctrl + T Tira a janela em foco da grade (ela fica onde está e as outras ocupam o espaço); apertar de novo devolve à grade
Win + Alt + F Modo foco: todas as janelas do monitor ocupam a tela toda; apertar de novo sai do modo
Win + Alt + ← / → Move a janela em foco para a esquerda / direita: troca de lugar com a janela vizinha daquele lado, qualquer que seja o layout (não faz nada se não houver)
Win + Alt + ↑ / ↓ Sobe / desce a janela em foco: troca de lugar com a janela logo acima / abaixo dela (não faz nada se não houver)
Win + Alt + Home Reorganiza tudo e devolve todas as janelas à grade

Todos os atalhos podem ser trocados nas configurações, e a mudança vale assim que você salva:

  • Layout, soltar/prender e reorganizar têm campos de texto próprios (por exemplo Ctrl+Alt+G, Win+T ou Alt+Home). Escreva os modificadores (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win) e uma tecla: uma letra, um dígito, ou Up, Down, Left, Right, Home ou End. Deixe o campo vazio para desligar o atalho.
  • Modo foco e as quatro setas compartilham uma única escolha de modificadores: Win+Alt (padrão), Ctrl+Alt, Ctrl+Alt+Shift ou Alt+Shift.
  • Evite combinações sem Win ou Ctrl: elas tiram a tecla de todos os outros apps.

Atalhos que não puderem ser registrados aparecem no log do Windhawk (erro 1409 = já em uso). Win + Alt + ↑ é um deles, a menos que você ligue Assumir atalhos (veja abaixo). Win + Ctrl + T também é o atalho padrão do Always On Top do PowerToys: se você usa os dois, troque um deles.

Assumir atalhos que já estão em uso

O próprio Windows usa algumas dessas combinações: Win + Alt + ↑ encaixa a janela na metade de cima da tela, então com as configurações padrão ela fica indisponível para o mod (o log mostra o erro 1409) e o Windows continua tratando-a. O mod nunca sobrescreve o atalho de outro programa se você não pedir. Para usar Win + Alt + ↑, ligue a opção Assumir atalhos (desligada por padrão) ou escolha outros modificadores para as setas. Com a opção ligada, sempre que um atalho já estiver ocupado o mod captura essa combinação com um gancho de teclado de baixo nível, e o outro programa ou o Windows deixa de recebê-la. O gancho roda numa thread própria, só existe enquanto o mod está ligado, e só para as combinações que já estavam ocupadas.

Menu radial: mover a janela com o mouse

Desligado por padrão. Nas configurações, escolha o botão que o abre: o botão direito, o do meio, ou Alt / Win + botão esquerdo. Depois pressione e segure esse botão sobre uma janela da grade. Um anel aparece onde o cursor está (depois de um instante, para não piscar num clique rápido). Mova o mouse para fora do anel, para a esquerda, direita, cima ou baixo: aquela fatia do anel acende e o espaço para onde a janela vai é destacado. Solte o botão para trocar a janela de lugar com a que ocupa aquele espaço. Esc cancela. Se não houver janela daquele lado, a fatia fica cinza e nada acontece. Só considera janelas do mesmo monitor.

O centro do anel solta e prende janelas sem o teclado. Mantenha o botão pressionado com o cursor parado: um pequeno círculo no meio se enche em cerca de meio segundo. Solte quando estiver cheio e a janela sai da grade (as outras ocupam o lugar dela). Faça o mesmo sobre uma janela solta e ela volta para a grade. Soltar antes de encher é um clique comum.

O anel tem três temas: Vidro líquido, o padrão (vidro transparente: a tela aparece nítida e se curva nas bordas do anel), Vidro (um tubo de vidro fosco que mostra a tela desfocada atrás dele) e Clássico (anel liso). A cor da seleção pinta a fatia escolhida e o destaque sobre a janela que vai receber a que você está movendo. Por padrão as cores são as da borda da janela em foco, acompanhando o efeito dela (pulsar, arco-íris, degradê); escolha Personalizadas para definir você mesmo a cor do anel e a cor da seleção. A espessura do anel também pode ser escolhida.

Se você soltar sem sair do anel, o clique é repassado ao app no momento em que o botão é solto, então um clique direito comum continua abrindo o menu de contexto. Sobre uma janela que o mod administra (na grade ou solta), arrastar com esse botão deixa de funcionar enquanto a opção está ligada; em qualquer outro lugar (a área de trabalho, a barra de tarefas, janelas maximizadas, apps ignorados) o clique nem é tocado. Ela precisa de um gancho de mouse de baixo nível, que só existe enquanto esta opção (ou um dos dois gestos com Alt, redimensionar ou mover) está ligada.

Funciona junto com outros mods de animação

O Adaptive Windows funciona junto com estes dois mods:

  • MacOS Minimize Animation (efeito genie ao minimizar, restaurar e abrir).

  • Windows Animations.

Esses mods escondem a janela e tocam a animação sozinhos. Com Sincronizar com animações de abrir/fechar ligado, o Adaptive Windows percebe isso, posiciona a janela no espaço final enquanto ela está escondida e anima só as outras janelas abrindo espaço, ao mesmo tempo. Cada janela tem uma única animação, sem briga.

Para o genie voltar ao lugar certo, enquanto uma janela está minimizada o mod grava no Windows o espaço que ela vai ocupar quando voltar e mantém esse valor atualizado conforme a grade muda. Assim a animação de restaurar termina onde a janela de fato vai ficar.

Programas que você excluir do outro mod (por exemplo, o Word no genie) não são animados por ele; nesse caso o Adaptive Windows usa a própria animação de entrada.

Animações

O estilo Nava OS é a base (curva de saída forte, janela nova entra deslizando da direita). Há também os estilos Suave (entra deslizando de cima), Rápido (sem efeito de entrada) e Elástico (entra de baixo com leve ressalto). Durante o movimento a janela mantém o tamanho (como ao arrastar): as que diminuem encolhem no início e as que crescem só crescem no final, sem sobreposição. A taxa de quadros pode seguir o DWM (recomendado), seguir a maior taxa de atualização entre os monitores, ou ser fixa (de 30 a 240 Hz).

Barra de tarefas e dock

A área útil é a área de trabalho do Windows. A Margem da borda da tela vale para os quatro lados. Se a barra de tarefas estiver escondida, as janelas respeitam apenas a borda da tela. Espaço embaixo (0 = automático) serve para docks desenhados por outro mod: informe a distância da borda da tela até o topo do dock. A barra de tarefas pode ficar em qualquer lado de qualquer monitor: a grade segue a área de trabalho do Windows e é refeita quando um monitor é conectado ou removido, a resolução muda, ou a barra é movida ou muda a opção de ocultar automaticamente.

Cantos

Usa a preferência de cantos do próprio Windows 11 (padrão, arredondado, pequeno, quadrado). O Windows não permite raio arbitrário por esta via. Se você já usa um mod de cantos (por exemplo, "Custom Window Corner Radius"), deixe esta opção em "Não mexer" para os dois não disputarem os cantos.

Janelas ignoradas e limites

  • As configurações valem assim que você as salva, sem reiniciar o mod. Mudar a lista de Aplicativos que ficam sempre fora da grade também tira janelas da grade (ou as traz) na hora.
  • Para tirar uma janela da grade por enquanto, use o atalho de soltar (Win + Ctrl + T). Para um aplicativo ficar sempre fora da grade, escreva o nome dele nessa lista (por exemplo spotify;chrome). Um nome vale se for o nome do programa ou se aparecer no título da janela. A lista vem vazia por padrão.
  • Janelas de ferramenta, sempre no topo, sem foco ou sem moldura redimensionável (por exemplo, painéis e widgets) ficam sempre fora da grade. O log do Windhawk diz por que cada janela foi ignorada.
  • Janelas que não aceitam ser posicionadas (um caso provável são programas executados como administrador) passam a flutuar depois de algumas tentativas; Win + Alt + Home tenta de novo.
  • Mover janelas pelo teclado só considera janelas do mesmo monitor.
